bug_semantics: Authenticated CWE-22 path traversal in Alist file-operation handlers. After the request directory is scoped to the caller's BasePath (originally stdpath.Join(user.BasePath, dir), later user.JoinPath which rejects '..' in the directory via utils.JoinBasePath), filename fields req.Names / renameObject.SrcName are concatenated with that directory using path.Join or fmt.Sprintf. Go path.Join cleans '..', so a name such as '../admin/private.txt' escapes the authorized directory and remove/copy/move/rename files belonging to other users on the same storage mount. PoC: POST /api/fs/remove with {"dir":"/","names":["../admin/private.txt"]}.
flaw_origin: First written in f275f83de02bc1f30f5dc2f766ea8c539816a8ee (2022-06-29, 'feat: fs manage api' by Noah Hsu <i@nn.ci>), which added server/controllers/fsmanage.go with FsRemove/FsCopy/FsMove joining unsanitized req.Names onto a user-scoped directory (FsRemove lines 129-131: req.Path = stdpath.Join(user.BasePath, req.Path); fs.Remove(c, stdpath.Join(req.Path, name))). Later JoinPath (b5bf5f43) and role-permission checks (00120cba) only validated the directory; FsBatchRename (258b8f52) later copied the same name-join via sprintf. The 2026 JoinUnderBase fix closed the original sink.
